judged_text: deleteEvent has the same tautological find: when externalCalendarId is falsy the predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` can never match, so calendarId resolves to undefined instead of the previous destinationCalendar.externalId fallback. Cancelling a legacy booking without a stored reference externalCalendarId no longer deletes the Google Calendar event (calendarId undefined → API error), leaving orphaned calendar events on every such cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the calendarId fallback as `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. When `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, that predicate can never match any real `cal.externalId`, so the fallback resolves to `undefined` instead of using the event’s destination calendar (previously `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, now likely the first element’s externalId). This is a real logic defect introduced by the array refactor and can break deletions/updates when no `externalCalendarId` is provided (e.g., legacy refs).
